slot.brief: From a given wave equation y = A sin(kx − ωt + φ), read off the amplitude, frequency, wavelength and wave speed.

stem: A travelling wave is described by $y=0.06\sin(4\pi x-20\pi t+\dfrac{\pi}{3})$, where $x$ and $y$ are in m and $t$ is in s. Which set gives $(A,f,\lambda,v)$?

verdicts.working: From the wave equation, A = 0.06 m, k = 4π rad/m, and ω = 20π rad/s. Thus λ = 2π/k = 0.50 m, f = ω/(2π) = 10 Hz, and v = fλ = 5 m/s.

working:
$A=0.06\ \text{m},\quad k=4\pi\ \text{rad m}^{-1},\quad \omega=20\pi\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$
$f=\dfrac{\omega}{2\pi}=10\ \text{Hz}$
$\lambda=\dfrac{2\pi}{k}=0.50\ \text{m}$
$v=\dfrac{\omega}{k}=5\ \text{m s}^{-1}$

Independent check: From the wave equation, A = 0.06 m, k = 4π rad/m, and ω = 20π rad/s. Thus λ = 2π/k = 0.50 m, f = ω/(2π) = 10 Hz, and v = fλ = 5 m/s.
solution:
Comparing with $y=A\sin(kx-\omega t+\phi)$ gives $A=0.06\ \text{m}$, $k=4\pi\ \text{rad m}^{-1}$ and $\omega=20\pi\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$. Thus
$$f=\frac{\omega}{2\pi}=10\ \text{Hz},\qquad \lambda=\frac{2\pi}{k}=0.50\ \text{m},\qquad v=\frac{\omega}{k}=5\ \text{m s}^{-1}.$$

draft.distractor_notes:
B: doubles the frequency by omitting the $2\pi$ conversion from angular frequency.
C: uses $\pi/k$ instead of $2\pi/k$ for wavelength, then calculates the corresponding speed.
D: uses $\omega$ instead of $\omega/k$ for wave speed.
